cues.en: This is the Global News Podcast from the BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 这里是 BBC World Service 的《Global News Podcast》。

cues.en: I'm Will Chalk and in the early hours of Wednesday, the 26th of August, these are our main stories.
cues.zh: 我是 Will Chalk。现在是8月26日星期三凌晨，以下是我们的主要新闻。

cues.en: Tributes are being paid to the Queen of Country and Western Music, Dolly Parton, who's died at the age of 80.
cues.zh: 人们纷纷悼念乡村与西部音乐女王多莉·帕顿，她去世时享年80岁。

cues.en: The head of Instagram, one of Meta's most popular platforms,
cues.zh: Instagram 负责人——Meta 最受欢迎的平台之一——

cues.en: denies encouraging employees to keep negative information away from the public at a high-stakes trial in the US.
cues.zh: 否认曾鼓励员工阻止负面信息公开。这场高风险审判正在美国进行。

cues.en: And the UN and Red Cross raise the alarm about so-called killer robots, autonomous drones that could use AI to attack and kill humans.
cues.zh: 联合国和红十字会也对所谓的“杀手机器人”发出警告：这类自主无人机可能利用人工智能攻击并杀死人类。

cues.en: They've declared it being absolutely fantastic and all the rest of it because that old, it could have lost its alcohol content...
cues.zh: 他们说酒质“绝对棒极了”，诸如此类；因为那酒年代久远，可能已经失去了酒精含量……

cues.en: How it feels to buy a whisky barrel for less than $200 and find out it's worth a fortune.
cues.zh: 花不到200美元买下一桶威士忌，却发现它价值连城，是什么感受？

cues.en: We're starting with one of the most important musicians of the past century, American singer Dolly Parton, who's died of cancer at the age of 80.
cues.zh: 首先关注上世纪最重要的音乐家之一、美国歌手多莉·帕顿；她因癌症去世，享年80岁。

cues.en: From poverty in rural Tennessee, she went on to become a global superstar,
cues.zh: 她出生于田纳西州乡村的贫困家庭，后来成为全球巨星；

cues.en: selling more than 100 million records, writing a whopping 3,000 songs in a career that spanned six decades.
cues.zh: 在长达六十年的职业生涯中，她卖出逾1亿张唱片，创作了惊人的3000首歌曲。

cues.en: There are dozens of hits we could name, but arguably the biggest ones are 9 to 5, I Will Always Love You, and Jolene.
cues.zh: 她的热门歌曲数不胜数，其中最知名的或许是《9 to 5》《I Will Always Love You》和《Jolene》。

cues.en: Her family released this video, with her nephew Bryan Seaver sharing the news.
cues.zh: 她的家人发布了这段视频，由她的外甥布莱恩·西弗公布消息。

cues.en: My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly. And so have you.
cues.zh: 我和家人与多莉共同度过了一生，留下了美好的回忆。你们也一样。

cues.en: She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family whether you liked it or not.
cues.zh: 无论你是否愿意，她一直出现在你的电视、唱片机、CD 和手机播放列表里，成为你家庭的一员。

cues.en: Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever.
cues.zh: 我们的家人，以及她托付遗产的团队，将竭尽全力确保她的精神永远与我们同在。

cues.en: Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy. He farmed the soil; she farmed songs and happiness.
cues.zh: 多莉和父亲一样，都是农民。他耕种土地，她耕种歌曲与幸福。

cues.en: Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton,
cues.zh: 多莉打电话告诉我，她想躺在漂亮的柔软棉花床上安息，

cues.en: because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest.
cues.zh: 因为一生都穿戴沉重的水钻服饰后，她终于值得舒适地休息一会儿。

cues.en: Rest in peace, Aunt Dolly, Aunt Granny, Gigi.
cues.zh: 安息吧，多莉姨妈、格兰妮姨妈、吉吉。

cues.en: May God bless Dolly Parton, and may God bless you all.
cues.zh: 愿上帝保佑多莉·帕顿，也愿上帝保佑大家。

cues.en: She will always love you.
cues.zh: 她永远爱着你们。

cues.en: Bryan Seaver there. Well, since the news broke of her death,
cues.zh: 以上是布莱恩·西弗的讲话。她去世的消息传出后，

cues.en: fans have been gathering in various places, including in Los Angeles, where Dolly Parton was given a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1984.
cues.zh: 各地粉丝纷纷聚集，包括洛杉矶；多莉·帕顿于1984年在那里获得了好莱坞星光大道上的一颗星。

cues.en: Our correspondent Shaimaa Khalil spoke to me from there.
cues.zh: 我们的记者沙伊玛·哈利勒从那里向我介绍了情况。

cues.en: It's a big gathering at Dolly Parton's star here on Hollywood Boulevard.
cues.zh: 好莱坞大道上多莉·帕顿的星星旁聚集了大批人。

cues.en: The star is barely visible, I tell you, because it is almost covered entirely now
cues.zh: 我告诉你，那颗星星几乎看不见了，因为现在几乎完全被覆盖，

cues.en: with bouquets of flowers, with pictures of Dolly Parton, with tributes and messages.
cues.zh: 上面摆满了花束、多莉·帕顿的照片，以及悼念和留言。

cues.en: One is saying, "Goodbye to our beloved American icon."
cues.zh: 一条留言写道：“再见了，我们深爱的美国偶像。”

cues.en: Another one saying, "We will always love you, Dolly."
cues.zh: 另一条写道：“多莉，我们永远爱你。”

cues.en: And there's a box of Dolly Parton sugar cookies, pink and red, very Dolly Parton style.
cues.zh: 还有一盒多莉·帕顿风格十足的糖霜饼干，粉红和红色相间。

cues.en: So many fans have been gathering around that star.
cues.zh: 许多粉丝一直聚集在那颗星星周围。

cues.en: I mean, this woman dedicated her whole life to bringing joy, comfort, happiness to the entire world, basically.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，这位女性倾尽一生，基本上为全世界带来了喜悦、慰藉和幸福。

cues.en: She could go into her own heart and write about the human experience,
cues.zh: 她能够深入自己的内心，写下关于人类经历的作品，

cues.en: whether it be joy or sorrow or heartache or vindictiveness.
cues.zh: 无论是喜悦、悲伤、心痛，还是报复心。

cues.en: And I will say that in a country that is so divided at the moment,
cues.zh: 我要说，在这个当下如此分裂的国家，

cues.en: Dolly Parton has been this really rare unifying figure across generations, across political affiliations.
cues.zh: 多莉·帕顿一直是极为罕见的团结力量，跨越不同世代和政治立场。

cues.en: You see that all the way from President Donald Trump, who talked about the loss, about the flag being taken to half-mast,
cues.zh: 从总统唐纳德·特朗普谈及这场离世、下半旗致哀一事，你就能看到这一点；

cues.en: the reactions from Hollywood, from celebrities, from the music industry, from the film industry,
cues.zh: 好莱坞、各界名人、音乐界和电影界都作出了回应，

cues.en: and from the fans here on the street where I'm standing.
cues.zh: 我所在这条街上的粉丝也不例外。

cues.en: There is just a common connection to her, a common love because of who she was and what she represented.
cues.zh: 大家只是因为她是谁、她代表什么，而与她有共同的联结和爱。

cues.en: Yeah, I mean, I was lucky enough to see Dolly Parton at Glastonbury Festival here in the UK in 2014,
cues.zh: 是啊，我曾有幸在2014年于英国这里的格拉斯顿伯里音乐节观看多莉·帕顿的演出，

cues.en: when I think she was in her...
cues.zh: 我记得那时她大概……

cues.en: Well, I think she was in her late sixties,
cues.zh: 嗯，我想她当时快七十岁了，

cues.en: but the number of teenagers and young people in the crowd—something about her, isn't there, that speaks to people whatever generation they are. And...
cues.zh: 但现场有那么多青少年和年轻人——她身上似乎有某种东西，能打动任何一代的人。而且……

cues.en: I was really surprised. I was speaking to a family who have come here from the UK, actually—a father and two of his daughters who are in their teens.
cues.zh: 我真的很惊讶。我采访了一家从英国来到这里的人——一位父亲和他的两个十几岁的女儿。

cues.en: I thought I was just going to speak to the dad, to Simon, about Dolly Parton,
cues.zh: 我原以为只会采访父亲西蒙，谈谈多莉·帕顿，

cues.en: and the two girls came up and said, ‘No, we want to speak about her as well.’
cues.zh: 没想到两个女孩也走过来说：“不，我们也想谈谈她。”

cues.en: One of them said, ‘I love her because of the causes that she has adopted,’ and another said, ‘I just love her music.’
cues.zh: 其中一个说：“我喜欢她，是因为她投身于公益事业。”另一个说：“我就是喜欢她的音乐。”

cues.en: There is something about her, about how she comes across, about how authentic she is, and you can feel it
cues.zh: 她身上有种特别之处：她给人的感觉，以及她的真诚，都能被人感受到，

cues.en: because a father in his forties or fifties is feeling the shock just as strongly as his teenage daughters.
cues.zh: 因为一位四五十岁的父亲和他十几岁的女儿一样，都深受这一消息冲击。

cues.en: A young twenty-one-year-old tells me how fun it was to dance to her music, to sing to her music,
cues.zh: 一位21岁的年轻人告诉我，伴着她的音乐跳舞、歌唱是多么快乐，

cues.en: but also how he felt every word when she was talking about how sad or lonely she is.
cues.zh: 但当她谈到自己的悲伤或孤独时，他也能真切感受到她说的每一个字。

cues.en: He felt that that was real, and I think that really crosses generations.
cues.zh: 他觉得那是真实的，我认为这确实跨越了世代。

cues.en: Shaimaa Khalil there.
cues.zh: 以上是沙伊玛·哈利勒的报道。

cues.en: Lydia Hamessley is a professor of music at Hamilton College in New York.
cues.zh: 莉迪娅·哈姆斯利是纽约汉密尔顿学院的音乐学教授。

cues.en: She's written the book Unlikely Angel: The Songs of Dolly Parton and featured in a landmark BBC documentary called Dolly Parton: Here I Am.
cues.zh: 她著有《意外的天使：多莉·帕顿的歌曲》，还参与了 BBC 里程碑式纪录片《多莉·帕顿：我就在这里》。

cues.en: James Coomarasamy asked her how it all began.
cues.zh: 詹姆斯·库马拉萨米询问她，这一切是如何开始的。

cues.en: She started writing songs as a child. She said her first song was when she was five years old, a little song called Little Tiny Tassel Top.
cues.zh: 她从小就开始写歌。她说自己的第一首歌是在五岁时写的，是一首叫《小小穗顶》的小歌。

cues.en: It was about her corn cob doll that her daddy made.
cues.zh: 那首歌写的是爸爸为她制作的玉米芯娃娃。

cues.en: Her mother recognized her songwriting talent and would write down the lyrics to the songs that Dolly made up as a child.
cues.zh: 她的母亲发现了她的歌曲创作天赋，会把多莉小时候编的歌的歌词记下来。

cues.en: So, you know, we're lucky that we have some of that.
cues.zh: 所以，我们很幸运，还保留着其中一些歌词。

cues.en: A corn cob doll that her father made—I think they paid the doctor in cornmeal when she was born.
cues.zh: 她父亲制作的玉米芯娃娃——我想，她出生时家人是用玉米粉支付医生费用的。

cues.en: I mean, that poverty in which she grew up, how key was it to her songwriting?
cues.zh: 她成长于那样的贫困之中，这对她的创作有多关键？

cues.en: Oh, I think it was absolutely central.
cues.zh: 我认为那绝对是核心因素。

cues.en: You know, she strikes me as being someone who has such a deep imagination that took her out of her poverty.
cues.zh: 她给我的感觉是，她拥有如此丰富的想象力，正是想象力带她走出了贫困。

cues.en: She has a song called Paradise Road that perhaps a lot of people don't know, but she sings in that song
cues.zh: 她有一首歌叫《天堂之路》，或许很多人并不知道，但她在歌中唱道：

cues.en: ‘Paradise is a state of mind. I can go there whenever I want.’
cues.zh: “天堂是一种心境，我想去的时候随时都能去。”

cues.en: I think that reflects probably the way she felt growing up, that she had to look for beauty
cues.zh: 我认为这或许反映了她成长时的感受：她必须去寻找美，

cues.en: where she could find it and had to use her imagination to kind of escape or to create a sense that was beyond the poverty.
cues.zh: 在能找到美的地方，并运用想象力逃离贫困，或者创造一种超越贫困的感受。

cues.en: She would talk about looking for broken glass out in the yard, which she would envision as jewels.
cues.zh: 她会说，自己在院子里寻找碎玻璃，并把它们想象成珠宝。

cues.en: She did become this, I mean, larger-than-life figure. I suppose it's fair to say.
cues.zh: 她确实成了一个——可以说——超凡脱俗的人物。

cues.en: Absolutely, and she talked about developing her look with the big hair, and that what she was trying to do was get attention
cues.zh: 确实如此。她说过，她用夸张的大头发打造自己的形象，目的是吸引注意力，

cues.en: in the '60s in Nashville when she went there to become a songwriter.
cues.zh: 那是她在20世纪60年代去纳什维尔当词曲作者时的做法。

cues.en: She wasn't thinking about becoming a singer as much as selling songs, but she knew she needed to get attention, and she thought,
cues.zh: 她当时想的不是成为歌手，而是卖歌；但她知道自己需要引起注意，于是想：

cues.en: ‘Well, this will get their attention. And then, once I've got their attention, maybe I can turn it to my songs.’
cues.zh: “好吧，这样就能吸引他们的注意。等他们注意到我，也许我就能让他们关注我的歌。”

cues.en: And you got her attention, didn't you? Because she actually contributed to your book, didn't she? Although not sort of face to face, right?
cues.zh: 而且你确实引起了她的注意，对吧？她还为你的书作了贡献，对吧？虽然不是面对面交流，是吗？

cues.en: I created a conversation that I wanted to participate in with her, and she was so generous to respond.
cues.zh: 我创造了一场想与她共同参与的对话，而她非常慷慨地作出了回应。

cues.en: I wanted to ask her things and talk with her about things that no one had done before.
cues.zh: 我想问她一些问题，和她谈论此前无人谈过的事情。

cues.en: So I really dug deeply into the music that she was writing, why she wrote the way she did, and what she thought about her songs.
cues.zh: 所以我深入研究了她创作的音乐、她为何以那种方式写歌，以及她如何看待自己的歌曲。

cues.en: She was lighthearted and very cheerful, but she took my questions so seriously, and I got a couple of real golden nuggets out of that conversation.
cues.zh: 她轻松风趣、非常愉快，却又极其认真地对待我的问题；那次对话让我获得了几颗真正的金玉良言。

cues.en: Oh well, what would you like to share?
cues.zh: 那么，你愿意分享些什么呢？

cues.en: Well, my favorite, although it's very much a music-nerdy kind of thing, is that I asked her about a particular chord that she uses in songs.
cues.zh: 我最喜欢的一点，虽然这属于音乐发烧友才会关注的内容，是我问她一种在歌曲中常用的特定和弦。

cues.en: It's a very specific kind of sound, and I said, ‘You use that a lot. Why do you like that?’
cues.zh: 那是一种非常特别的声音。我说：“你经常使用这种和弦，为什么喜欢它？”

cues.en: And she said, ‘Oh yeah, I know what you mean about that.’ She said, ‘Well, that's just that old sorrow chord, isn't it?’
cues.zh: 她说：“哦，对，我知道你说的是什么。”她说：“那就是老式的‘悲伤和弦’，不是吗？”

cues.en: My heart just melted when I heard her say that. I thought that whole interview was worth it to hear her describe this chord as the sorrow chord.
cues.zh: 听到她这么说，我的心都融化了。我觉得，能听她把这个和弦称作“悲伤和弦”，那次采访就完全值得了。

cues.en: And as you say, the wit, but also the seriousness, and I guess that seriousness manifested itself both in her business acumen and in her philanthropy.
cues.zh: 正如你所说，她既机智又严肃；我想，这种严肃既体现在她的商业头脑上，也体现在她的慈善事业中。

cues.en: Oh yes, she definitely was interested in giving back to her community and then spreading it much wider with the Imagination Library
cues.zh: 是的，她确实热衷于回馈社区，后来又通过“想象图书馆”把这份事业推广到更广的地方，

cues.en: that started very locally in her Sevier County but then, you know, has travelled worldwide.
cues.zh: 这个项目最初只在她所在的塞维尔县开展，后来推广到了全世界。

cues.en: A lot of her philanthropy, I think, people aren't aware of. Most people know of the library and the COVID funding for the Moderna shot,
cues.zh: 我想，她的许多慈善行动并不为人所知。大多数人知道她的图书馆项目，以及她为莫德纳新冠疫苗提供的资金，

cues.en: but also money for the wildfires that happened—I think it was 2016—in eastern Tennessee,
cues.zh: 但她还为东田纳西州的那场山火提供了资金——我想那是在2016年，

cues.en: and also funding a birthing unit at the local hospital there in Sevier County.
cues.zh: 并资助了塞维尔县当地医院的产科病房。

cues.en: I have a feeling that we may learn a lot more about the philanthropy that she did that we just don't know of yet.
cues.zh: 我感觉，我们或许还会了解到更多她所做的、目前尚不为我们所知的慈善事业。

cues.en: Lydia Hamessley speaking to James Coomarasamy.
cues.zh: 莉迪娅·哈姆斯利接受詹姆斯·库马拉萨米采访。

cues.en: For more than a week, Meta—the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp—has been on federal trial in California.
cues.zh: 一个多星期来，Meta（Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp 的所有者）在加州接受联邦审判。

cues.en: The company is accused of deliberately designing features that get children addicted.
cues.zh: 该公司被控故意设计让儿童上瘾的功能。

cues.en: On Tuesday, the high-profile court case brought by 29 US states heard from its first top executive from the company.
cues.zh: 周二，由美国 29 个州提起的这起高调案件，听取了该公司首位高层主管的证词。

cues.en: Instagram's boss Adam Mosseri denied that he'd encourage employees to hide negative information from the public.
cues.zh: Instagram 负责人亚当·莫塞里否认自己会鼓励员工向公众隐瞒负面信息。

cues.en: Our North America technology correspondent Lily Jamali told me more about Mr Mosseri's highly anticipated appearance.
cues.zh: 本台北美科技记者莉莉·贾马利向我介绍了备受期待的莫塞里出庭作证。

cues.en: Yeah, it was pretty riveting, actually—quite a lively set of exchanges.
cues.zh: 是的，确实相当扣人心弦，双方交锋十分激烈。

cues.en: They were between a lawyer for the Colorado Attorney General's Office and Adam Mosseri, of course, the head of Instagram.
cues.zh: 交锋双方是一名代表科罗拉多州总检察长办公室的律师，以及 Instagram 负责人亚当·莫塞里。

cues.en: A lot of time was spent talking about the flow of information inside Meta.
cues.zh: 大量时间都在讨论 Meta 内部的信息流动。

cues.en: Who gets to see what, and how much do they get to see when they're able to access, for example, research on sensitive topics.
cues.zh: 谁能看到什么，以及他们在能够查阅敏感议题研究时，究竟能看到多少。

cues.en: So that was really the main focus today. So you touched on it a little bit there.
cues.zh: 所以这确实是今天的重点。你刚才也稍微提到了这一点。

cues.en: You know, some of what was asked by the Attorney General's Office in Colorado was about what information makes it to Adam Mosseri himself.
cues.zh: 科罗拉多州总检察长办公室提出的问题，有一部分涉及哪些信息会传到亚当·莫塞里本人那里。

cues.en: Because we had earlier seen in internal documents some chats among Meta employees, including some fairly high-level employees.
cues.zh: 因为我们此前在内部文件中看到过 Meta 员工之间的一些聊天记录，其中包括一些级别相当高的员工。

cues.en: Those chats showed employees were careful not to reveal too much to Adam Mosseri, potentially because of the legal risk they might put him in.
cues.zh: 这些聊天记录显示，员工非常谨慎，不愿向亚当·莫塞里透露过多信息，可能是因为那会让他面临法律风险。

cues.en: And then we also heard talk of what employees get to see internally of this very sensitive research that happens.
cues.zh: 此外，我们还听到了员工在内部能看到哪些此类敏感研究的讨论。

cues.en: After the Facebook files' release—remember, in 2021 a whistleblower released internal company documents first published in the Wall Street Journal.
cues.zh: “Facebook 文件”发布后——记得吗，2021 年一名举报人披露了公司内部文件，最先由《华尔街日报》刊出。

cues.en: Well, after that incident happened, they started to limit who could see research.
cues.zh: 那起事件发生后，他们开始限制谁能够查看研究。

cues.en: He said it was important to ensure they no longer gave access to people who didn't work on particular projects, really limiting the scope.
cues.zh: 他谈到，重要的是确保不再让不参与特定项目的人获得访问权限，从而大幅限制访问范围。

cues.en: And what are these US states ultimately hoping to get out of this?
cues.zh: 那么，这些美国州最终希望从中得到什么？

cues.en: Two things: they want Meta to pay a lot of money, and they want the company to make changes.
cues.zh: 两点：他们希望 Meta 支付巨额款项，也希望公司作出改变。

cues.en: So, on that first point, I've talked to California Attorney General Rob Bonta about what exactly is the sum that they're looking for.
cues.zh: 先说第一点，我采访了加州总检察长罗布·邦塔，询问他们具体要求多少赔偿。

cues.en: He wouldn't put a number on it. He said it would be a significant request if they're able to succeed in this first phase of the trial.
cues.zh: 他不愿给出具体数字。他说，如果他们能在审判第一阶段胜诉，要求的金额将会很高。

cues.en: I've seen reports from $400 billion to as high as $1.4 trillion, which is nearly the amount that Wall Street values Meta as a company.
cues.zh: 报道估计金额从4000亿美元到最高1.4万亿美元不等，后者几乎相当于华尔街对Meta整家公司的估值。

cues.en: But we won't know until the states, if and only if they win, get to the second phase.
cues.zh: 但要等这些州胜诉并进入第二阶段后，我们才会知道。

cues.en: They also want the company, as I mentioned, to make changes to features like infinite scroll and notifications.
cues.zh: 正如我提到的，他们还希望公司修改无限滚动和通知等功能。

cues.en: These are things that pull young users back onto their apps, even after they've left.
cues.zh: 这些功能会把年轻用户吸引回应用，即使他们已经离开。

cues.en: And we should note, from Meta's perspective.
cues.zh: 不过也应注意，从 Meta 的角度来看，

cues.en: They say that they have tried to be an industry leader in dealing with the issue of youth harm,
cues.zh: 他们说，自己一直努力成为应对青少年伤害问题的行业领导者，

cues.en: and that they've used the research they've done to improve the product, to create tools that can help, for example, teenagers with time management.
cues.zh: 并利用开展的研究改进产品，创建工具来帮助青少年管理时间等。

cues.en: Lily Jamali there in San Francisco.
cues.zh: 莉莉·贾马利从旧金山发回报道。

cues.en: Let's move on to a warning from the United Nations and the Red Cross.
cues.zh: 下面来看联合国和红十字国际委员会发出的警告。

cues.en: The world, we're told, is dangerously close to having fully autonomous weapons that can kill humans.
cues.zh: 据警告，世界正危险地接近拥有能够杀死人的完全自主武器。

cues.en: They've repeated their appeal for international regulation of what some are calling killer robots.
cues.zh: 他们再次呼吁对一些人所谓的“杀手机器人”进行国际监管。

cues.en: Alessandra Vellucci is the director of the UN Information Service in Geneva.
cues.zh: 亚历山德拉·韦卢奇是联合国日内瓦新闻处处长。

cues.en: Three years ago, we called on states to establish specific provisions and restrictions on autonomous weapon systems.
cues.zh: 三年前，我们呼吁各国为自主武器系统制定具体条款和限制。

cues.en: Today, we renew this call with even greater urgency. The fundamental concerns remain unchanged.
cues.zh: 今天，我们以更加紧迫的态度重申这一呼吁。根本担忧并未改变。

cues.en: But the risks have intensified. We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines.
cues.zh: 但风险已经加剧。我们如今危险地接近一道道德红线：由机器自主锁定人类目标。

cues.en: That warning comes in the same week that The New York Times reported a Russian drone, which killed three people in Ukraine last month,
cues.zh: 发出这一警告的同一周，《纽约时报》报道称，一架上月在乌克兰杀死三人的俄罗斯无人机，

cues.en: appeared to choose its own target using artificial intelligence.
cues.zh: 似乎利用人工智能自行选择了目标。

cues.en: Andrew Kramer wrote that article about the Russian AI-guided drones being tested in southern Ukraine.
cues.zh: 安德鲁·克莱默撰写了这篇报道，介绍在乌克兰南部测试的俄罗斯人工智能制导无人机。

cues.en: What we found were weapons that had been designed without antennas, with no human in the loop.
cues.zh: 我们发现的是没有配备天线、没有人在决策环节中的武器。

cues.en: They had small computers that would guide them to a target,
cues.zh: 它们配有能将其引导至目标的小型计算机，

cues.en: and the AI computer, which was on board, would decide whether to strike or not.
cues.zh: 机载人工智能计算机会决定是否发动攻击。

cues.en: And it's chilling because it raised the prospect of a computer making a lethal decision.
cues.zh: 这令人不寒而栗，因为它意味着计算机可能作出生死攸关的决定。

cues.en: It's distinct from previous generations of weapons where they had a human-programmed computer,
cues.zh: 这不同于以往几代武器，后者配备的是由人类编程的计算机，

cues.en: but these small computers were using machine learning to determine whether a target fit their category or not,
cues.zh: 而这些小型计算机利用机器学习来判断目标是否符合其类别，

cues.en: and it really is a Pandora's box for the use of AI in weaponry.
cues.zh: 这确实为人工智能在武器中的应用打开了潘多拉魔盒。

cues.en: They are assembled in a number of countries, including in China, and the computer boards we looked at said, "made in China."
cues.zh: 它们在包括中国在内的多个国家组装；我们查看的电脑板上写着“产自中国”。

cues.en: We don't know how the Russians obtain them, but they're widely available in the world.
cues.zh: 我们不知道俄罗斯人如何获得这些设备，但它们在全球广泛供应。

cues.en: The concern is that these machine-learning systems are studying war, and that the future will really bring an arsenal of AI weaponry.
cues.zh: 令人担忧的是，这些机器学习系统正在研究战争，而未来真的会带来一个人工智能武器库。

cues.en: They will become more sophisticated and be able to target humans, perhaps distinguishing a soldier from a civilian.
cues.zh: 它们会变得更加先进，能够瞄准人类，或许还能区分士兵和平民。

cues.en: They will be competent in striking vehicles on roads and other targets, and can be produced quite cheaply in large numbers.
cues.zh: 它们将能有效打击道路上的车辆和其他目标，而且可以以相当低的成本大量生产。

cues.en: Andrew Kramer. Our global affairs reporter Paul Moss has more about this call to action from the UN and the Red Cross.
cues.zh: 安德鲁·克莱默。我们的全球事务记者保罗·莫斯将介绍联合国和红十字会发出的这一行动呼吁。

cues.en: What the United Nations is saying is that, look, we've been warning about the dangers of autonomously driven weapon systems for a long time,
cues.zh: 联合国的意思是：我们一直在警告自主驱动武器系统的危险，已经很久了。

cues.en: but now the reality is that these are coming closer than ever.
cues.zh: 但现实是，这些武器如今比以往任何时候都更接近我们。

cues.en: Drones have already caused devastation in places like Ukraine, and they have pinpoint accuracy.
cues.zh: 无人机已经在乌克兰等地造成破坏，而且打击精度极高。

cues.en: We know that they can destroy a particular building, or they can hit a particular floor of a building.
cues.zh: 我们知道，它们可以摧毁一栋特定建筑，也可以击中建筑的某一层。

cues.en: But what an AI drone can do is to make a decision by itself.
cues.zh: 但人工智能无人机能够自行作出决定。

cues.en: For example, you could send it off and give it a car number plate and say,
cues.zh: 比如，你可以派出无人机，给它一块车牌，然后说：

cues.en: "Find this car wherever it is and then destroy it."
cues.zh: “找到这辆车，不管它在哪里，然后摧毁它。”

cues.en: You could give it a face, and with facial-recognition software, it could find a particular person or recognize a particular uniform.
cues.zh: 你可以给它一张脸；借助人脸识别软件，它能找到某个人，或识别某种制服。

cues.en: Once sent off, it would be able to make a decision for itself.
cues.zh: 一旦被派出去，它就能自行作出决定。

cues.en: And of course, part of the risk that the United Nations has been warning about is that this can go wrong.
cues.zh: 当然，联合国一直警告的风险之一，就是这一切可能出错。

cues.en: Anyone who's used AI domestically will have had the experience of asking a personal or perhaps very simple question,
cues.zh: 任何在日常生活中使用过人工智能的人，都可能问过一个私人问题，或者一个很简单的问题，

cues.en: and getting a completely false answer—a so-called hallucination.
cues.zh: 却得到完全错误的答案——所谓的“幻觉”。

cues.en: Well, what if an AI-armed system was to make that sort of error?
cues.zh: 那么，如果一套人工智能武器系统犯下那种错误呢？

cues.en: The possible consequences are terrifying. Paul Moss.
cues.zh: 可能造成的后果令人恐惧。以上是保罗·莫斯的报道。

cues.en: This is the Global News Podcast. Canada's announced tit-for-tat tariffs on billions of dollars' worth of imports,
cues.zh: 这里是《Global News Podcast》。加拿大宣布对价值数十亿美元的进口商品征收报复性关税，

cues.en: from the United States, as the trade war between the two countries escalates.
cues.zh: 这些进口商品来自美国；随着两国贸易战升级，

cues.en: Talks about a deal collapsed last week.
cues.zh: 有关协议的谈判上周破裂。

cues.en: The Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said his country had been attacked by the US and was at war with it.
cues.zh: 加拿大总理马克·卡尼说，他的国家遭到美国攻击，正与美国交战。

cues.en: President Trump imposed steep levies on Monday, with Canada saying it would match them.
cues.zh: 特朗普总统周一征收高额关税，加拿大表示将予以匹配。

cues.en: Here's our senior North America correspondent, Gary O'Donoghue.
cues.zh: 以下是我们的北美资深记者加里·奥多诺休的报道。

cues.en: After talks broke down, Canada promised to respond dollar-for-dollar to Donald Trump's tariffs, and that's precisely what it has done.
cues.zh: 谈判破裂后，加拿大承诺以对等规模反制唐纳德·特朗普的关税，而它确实这样做了。

cues.en: Canadian levies on American farm equipment, dairy, paper and electronics, among other things,
cues.zh: 加拿大对美国农用设备、乳制品、纸张和电子产品等征收的关税，

cues.en: will come into force on the 8th of September, on a sliding scale from 15 up to 50%.
cues.zh: 将于9月8日生效，税率从15%逐步升至50%。

cues.en: Steel and aluminium, already facing a 25% tariff, will now jump to 50%, matching Washington's own levy.
cues.zh: 钢铁和铝此前已面临25%的关税，如今将升至50%，与华盛顿的税率相同。

cues.en: And crucially, they say, there's room to go further if Washington escalates again.
cues.zh: 更重要的是，他们说，如果华盛顿再次升级，关税还有进一步上调的空间。

cues.en: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne says it's an unprecedented challenge imposed on Canada.
cues.zh: 财政部长弗朗索瓦-菲利普·尚帕涅说，这是加拿大遭遇的前所未有的挑战。

cues.en: The terms proposed by the US administration were uneconomic, unfair, and ultimately, unacceptable.
cues.zh: 美国政府提出的条件不合乎经济原则、不公平，最终也不可接受。

cues.en: They asked too much of Canada and offered too little in return.
cues.zh: 他们向加拿大索取太多，作为回报却给得太少。

cues.en: Donald Trump's tariffs had already drawn strong reactions from some Canadian politicians.
cues.zh: 特朗普的关税已经引发一些加拿大政界人士的强烈反应。

cues.en: Doug Ford is the premier of Ontario, with a blunt message.
cues.zh: 安大略省省长道格·福特的表态十分直白。

cues.en: This guy's a loser. We're going to fight with everything we have. I have more courage, more brains in my baby toe than he has in his whole body.
cues.zh: 这家伙是个失败者。我们会竭尽全力抗争。我小脚趾里的勇气和智慧都比他全身上下的多。

cues.en: For Republicans in the US, the timing could hardly be worse, with midterm elections looming and the cost of living uppermost in voters' minds.
cues.zh: 对美国共和党来说，时机几乎糟糕透顶：中期选举将近，而生活成本是选民最关心的问题。

cues.en: Several of the states most exposed to Canadian trade—Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Alaska—are also home to some very tight US Senate races.
cues.zh: 几个最容易受到加拿大贸易影响的州——缅因、密歇根、俄亥俄和阿拉斯加——也正举行竞争非常激烈的美国参议院选举。

cues.en: Canada says it's ready to go back to the negotiating table.
cues.zh: 加拿大表示准备重返谈判桌。

cues.en: But Donald Trump has vented his anger several times on social media, branding his northern neighbour entitled and unreasonable.
cues.zh: 但唐纳德·特朗普多次在社交媒体上发泄怒火，称这个北方邻国自以为是、蛮不讲理。

cues.en: And he has floated renaming Lake Ontario, which borders New York State, as Lake America.
cues.zh: 他还提出把与纽约州接壤的安大略湖改名为“美国湖”。

cues.en: There seems little sign that either side is about to blink in this increasingly acrimonious dispute.
cues.zh: 在这场日益尖锐的争端中，双方似乎都没有退让的迹象。

cues.en: On to a question that's at the heart of journalism: when does the drive for a scoop discourage people from telling the truth?
cues.zh: 接下来谈一个新闻业的核心问题：对独家新闻的追求何时会让人不愿讲真话？

cues.en: Well, it's a question that Tracy Scott-Wilson has explored in a new play called The Story.
cues.zh: 特蕾西·斯科特-威尔逊在新剧《The Story》中探讨了这个问题。

cues.en: Nicola Stanbridge went along to rehearsals at the National Theatre here in London, where the play opens this week.
cues.zh: 尼古拉·斯坦布里奇前往伦敦国家剧院的排练现场，该剧本周在这里开演。

cues.en: Rehearsing the gripping opening of The Story: the murder of a white teacher in a Black neighbourhood.
cues.zh: 他们正在排练《The Story》扣人心弦的开场：一名白人教师在黑人社区遭到谋杀。

cues.en: What, we're lost again? We're not!
cues.zh: 什么，我们又迷路了？没有！

cues.en: Yes, we are! He said to turn right, two blocks...
cues.zh: 不，我们就是迷路了！他说要右转，走两个街区……

cues.en: They wanted to show their parents the area had changed.
cues.zh: 他们想让父母看看这个地区已经变了。

cues.en: They wanted to show their parents it wasn't so dangerous.
cues.zh: 他们想让父母看看这里并没有那么危险。

cues.en: We are lost!
cues.zh: 我们迷路了！

cues.en: Playwright Tracy Scott-Wilson and director Clint Dyer explore how the story is reported by an ambitious young reporter.
cues.zh: 剧作家特蕾西·斯科特-威尔逊与导演克林特·戴尔探讨一名雄心勃勃的年轻记者如何报道这个故事。

cues.en: A journalist who is writing about a very high-profile, contentious news story and its repercussions in the community.
cues.zh: 一名记者正在报道一则备受关注、颇具争议的新闻，以及它在社区中造成的影响。

cues.en: Yvonne is the young hot-shot journalist.
cues.zh: 伊冯是那位年轻的明星记者。

cues.en: Usually, you take your time to move up the ranks, but Yvonne wants everything now in her own way.
cues.zh: 通常，人们会花时间逐步晋升，但Yvonne想要按照自己的方式立刻得到一切。

cues.en: Every time I bring a story back, Pat edits it to death. She says it's not positive enough.
cues.zh: 我每次带回一篇报道，帕特都会把它改得面目全非。她说报道不够积极。

cues.en: Are you sure about your sources here?
cues.zh: 你确定这里的消息来源可靠吗？

cues.en: Girlfriend's been in town for five minutes; she's built no relationships, no trust, no sources, but she's trying to be Woodward and Bernstein.
cues.zh: 姑娘来这个镇子才五分钟；她没有建立任何关系、赢得任何信任，也没有消息来源，却跑来这里想当伍德沃德和伯恩斯坦。

cues.en: In part inspired by Janet Cooke's 1980 Washington Post story.
cues.zh: 这部剧的部分灵感来自珍妮特·库克于1980年在《华盛顿邮报》发表的报道。

cues.en: She won a Pulitzer Prize for a story that turned out to be fabricated, but it veers very far from that.
cues.zh: 她曾凭一篇后来被证实造假的报道赢得普利策奖，但这部剧与那件事相去甚远。

cues.en: She just came back to her editors and said that she found this kid who was a heroin addict.
cues.zh: 她只是回去告诉编辑，说自己找到了一个吸食海洛因的孩子。

cues.en: This was the beginning of the crack era. They went with it, and had she not won the Pulitzer, there's a good chance she wouldn't have been caught.
cues.zh: 那是可卡因危机时代的开始。他们采用了这篇报道；如果她没有赢得普利策奖，很可能就不会被揭穿。

cues.en: It led to changes in newsroom standards and this public apology from Janet Cooke on ABC's Nightline.
cues.zh: 这件事促使新闻编辑部的标准发生改变，也促成了珍妮特·库克在美国广播公司《夜线》节目中的公开道歉。

cues.en: Regardless of what happened to me at the Post, I can never offer that as an excuse for what I did. It was wrong. I shouldn't have done it.
cues.zh: 不管我在《邮报》经历了什么，我都不能把那当作自己所作所为的借口。那是错误的，我不该那样做。

cues.en: For the rest of my life, I'm going to have to deal with people who are not going to believe a thing I say about practically anything.
cues.zh: 我的余生都必须面对这样的人：他们几乎不会相信我说的任何事情。

cues.en: This has been happening since the dawn of newspapers.
cues.zh: 这种情况从报纸诞生之初就一直存在。

cues.en: It always ends up being a systemic failure of the paper, for whatever reasons, culturally or politically. Why is it relevant now, do you think?
cues.zh: 无论出于文化还是政治等原因，最终总会演变成报纸自身的系统性失败。你觉得这在如今为什么仍然重要？

cues.en: We're in a time when everyone has the capability to be their own newspaper.
cues.zh: 我们身处这样一个时代：每个人都有能力成为自己的报纸。

cues.en: And we always deliver the news via our own perspective.
cues.zh: 而我们总是通过自己的视角传递新闻。

cues.en: And this story is about who suffers from that.
cues.zh: 而这个故事讲的就是谁会因此受苦。

cues.en: The Yvonne character is an outsider.
cues.zh: Yvonne这个角色是个局外人。

cues.en: There are thousands of journalists from all different backgrounds who report faithfully.
cues.zh: 有成千上万来自不同背景的记者在忠实地报道。

cues.en: As faithfully as they can, as faithfully as the outlet that they work for allows them to be.
cues.zh: 他们尽可能忠实，也忠实到供职媒体所允许的程度。

cues.en: We have to be very meticulous. Your job is to gather, disseminate and verify information. Nothing more.
cues.zh: 我们必须一丝不苟。你的工作就是收集、传播并核实信息，仅此而已。

cues.en: A clip from the play called The Story, ending that report by Nicola Stanbridge.
cues.zh: 以上是剧作《The Story》的片段，尼古拉·斯坦布里奇的报道到此结束。

cues.en: Right, we are nearly done, but before we go, how does this sound for a return on your investment?
cues.zh: 好了，节目快结束了。不过在此之前，听听你的投资回报如何？

cues.en: £130 in, nearly £270,000 out.
cues.zh: 投入130英镑，回报接近27万英镑。

cues.en: It would be a pretty good feeling, wouldn't it? Arguably even better if the investment was one that you'd forgotten you'd ever made.
cues.zh: 这感觉一定很棒，对吧？要是你早已忘记自己做过这笔投资，感觉或许会更好。

cues.en: Well, get ready to be jealous of Angus Kerr from southern England.
cues.zh: 好了，准备羡慕一下来自英格兰南部的安格斯·克尔吧。

cues.en: He invested in a barrel of whisky 50 years ago. It slipped his mind for decades, and he's just found out it's worth a fortune.
cues.zh: 50年前，他投资买下一桶威士忌。几十年来他把这件事忘在脑后，如今才发现它价值不菲。

cues.en: Lucy Aitchison reports. Angus Kerr bought the Glenrothes single malt in 1971, hoping to sell it five years later to pay his children's school fees.
cues.zh: 露西·艾奇逊报道：安格斯·克尔于1971年买下这桶格兰路思单一麦芽威士忌，希望五年后卖掉它来支付孩子们的学费。

cues.en: But the company went bust and he lost track of where the barrel was being stored.
cues.zh: 但公司破产了，他也不知道酒桶被存放在何处。

cues.en: Fast-forward more than 50 years, and the 81-year-old finally decided to hunt it down and put it on the market.
cues.zh: 50多年过去，如今81岁的他终于决定找回酒桶，把它推向市场。

cues.en: There's enough whisky inside the barrel for around 287 bottles, and he was in for quite a surprise when experts tasted it.
cues.zh: 这桶酒足够装约287瓶；专家品尝后，结果让他大吃一惊。

cues.en: The luck of it. I didn't realise they'd declared it absolutely fantastic and all the rest of it.
cues.zh: 真是幸运。我没想到他们会说这酒好得不得了，诸如此类。

cues.en: At that age, it could have lost its alcohol content. Also, the taste could have ended up being very oaky and horrible.
cues.zh: 酒到了那个年份，酒精度可能已经降得很低，味道也可能变得橡木味过重、难以下咽。

cues.en: Angus already has plans: a trip to Australia with his wife to visit their extended family.
cues.zh: Angus已经有了计划：和妻子去澳大利亚探望大家庭成员。

cues.en: His now grown-up children have given him eight grandchildren.
cues.zh: 他已经成年的孩子们为他带来了八个孙辈。

cues.en: And Angus admits the rest of the money might not stay in the bank for long.
cues.zh: Angus承认，剩下的钱可能不会在银行里存太久。

cues.en: Lucy Aitchison.
cues.zh: 露西·艾奇逊。

cues.en: That's all from us for now. If you want to get in touch, you can email us at globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk.
cues.zh: 以上就是本期节目。如果想联系我们，可以发送邮件至globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk。

cues.en: You can also find us on X at BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 你也可以在X上关注BBC World Service。

cues.en: This edition of the Global News Podcast was mixed by Rowan Morrison and the producer was Emma Joseph.
cues.zh: 本期《Global News Podcast》由罗文·莫里森混音，制片人是艾玛·约瑟夫。

cues.en: The editor is Karen Martin, and I'm Will Chalk.
cues.zh: 编辑是凯伦·马丁，我是威尔·乔克。

cues.en: Until next time, goodbye.
cues.zh: 下期再见。
